overview.problem: A reconstruction over two collections sharing tracks whose tags diverge refuses the whole write: assemble_output returns output None with the bare token unresolved_conflicts, the page renders that token and discards the conflict rows the run already computed, and the write control then reports 'Preview first' for a preview that ran and refused.
overview.approach: Keep DL-008's abort as what an undecided divergence does and make resolution additive: _resolve_conflicts and assemble_output take a named resolutions mapping from identity key to base or source, defaulting empty, alongside the run-wide on_conflict they already take. The decisions, the row projection, the bulk actions and the write-refusal reason live in a nicegui-free traktor_nml/gui/conflict_model.py mirroring review_model.py and wizard_state.py; the /reconstruct page renders hand-rolled ui.row rows against them. The screen is drawn into Specs first and built to. Two cheap unblocks - the conflict rows rendered in place of the bare token and a run-wide conflict choice on the page - stand ahead of the rest inside the page milestone, which shares app.py with them. The splice subcommand keeps only its run-wide flag. The target repository keeps its own decision log in traktor_nml/README.md at high-water mark DL-103, so this plan mints from DL-104.

decisions.decision: Per-key conflict resolutions reach the core as a named resolutions mapping on _resolve_conflicts and assemble_output, keyed by the identity-group key, valued base or source; the run-wide on_conflict parameter keeps its meaning and applies only where no per-key entry names that group
decisions.reasoning: _resolve_conflicts already computes one ConflictRow per divergent group and already carries the identity key that names it -> a per-key mapping needs no new grouping pass and no second identity notion, only a lookup at the point the abort is raised -> the mapping is added as a named keyword parameter and the widened return is a named element, never an appended positional, with every caller enumerated by grep first (assemble_output in traktor_nml/splice.py, _handle_splice in traktor_nml/commands/splice_cmd.py, the direct uses in tests/test_splice.py and the GUI call in traktor_nml/gui/app.py), following DL-100's precedent

decisions.decision: A group carrying divergent attributes with neither a per-key resolution nor a run-wide on_conflict keeps DL-008's abort exactly: output is None, errors carries unresolved_conflicts, conflict_rows is populated, and nothing is written
decisions.reasoning: DL-008's abort exists because _resolve_conflicts picks one winner per group, so resolving a divergence arbitrarily writes a plausible but wrong collection -> a per-key mapping supplies a winner the operator named rather than one the tool guessed, which is the only thing that makes writing safe -> resolution is additive and the abort remains the behaviour for every group nobody has decided, so the shape DL-008 named is extended rather than replaced and a run with an empty mapping is byte-identical to one made without the parameter

decisions.decision: The conflict decision state and the row derivation live in traktor_nml/gui/conflict_model.py, a nicegui-free module, mirroring review_model.py and wizard_state.py's split of what the tool found from what the operator said
decisions.reasoning: DL-069 puts every rule worth testing below the nicegui boundary because the suite's system interpreter has no nicegui -> resolution logic placed in app.py would be unreachable from the suite and would fail tests/test_gui_view_boundary.py's AST walk -> conflict_model.py holds ConflictDecisions (per identity key: undecided, base, source), the row projection over a ConflictRow plus its decision, the bulk all-base/all-source application, and the outstanding count, and imports no nicegui

decisions.decision: Per-track picks are held in session state keyed by the identity key, surviving a re-preview after an output path change or an added source, and lost on app restart
decisions.reasoning: the identity key is what _resolve_conflicts groups on and what ConflictRow already carries, so it is stable across two runs over the same inputs -> keying decisions on it lets a re-preview re-attach every decision without a second identifier or a sidecar file -> ConflictDecisions is held beside the /reconstruct page's other holders, discarded with the process, matching how state.decisions holds the reconnect flow's picks

decisions.decision: The splice CLI keeps only the run-wide --on-conflict keep-first|keep-last flag; the per-key resolutions parameter has the GUI as its sole caller
decisions.reasoning: a per-key mapping expressed on a command line needs a file format, a parser and a report of keys that matched nothing -> that surface serves no operator the tool has, since the operator resolving track-by-track is the one looking at rendered rows -> splice_cmd.py passes no resolutions and its argument list is unchanged, and the core's default of an empty mapping keeps the CLI path identical

decisions.decision: The conflict-resolution screen is drawn into design/reconnect-wizard/Specs.dc.html before it is built, and built to what Specs then says
decisions.reasoning: DL-071 makes Specs the cross-screen contract for what the operator sees, and a screen disagreeing with Specs is fixed in Specs -> a screen Specs has never described would either carve an exception to that rule or be reconciled after the fact against a contract written to match the code -> Specs gains the conflict screen first, so the page is built to a contract that already exists

decisions.decision: The conflict table renders hand-rolled ui.row rows per conflicting track, one row showing the base version against the source version with a base/source pick, alongside run-wide all-base and all-source actions
decisions.reasoning: DL-079 rejected ui.aggrid for the review table because aggrid claims the arrow keys Specs binds over that same table -> the conflict table sits in the same wizard surface under the same keyboard contract, so adopting aggrid here would reintroduce exactly that collision -> rows are hand-rolled the way the review step's rows are, and a conflict set of hundreds of rows is made tractable by bulk actions rather than by a grid widget

decisions.decision: The write control refuses on a reason the model returns, distinguishing a preview that never ran from a preview that ran and refused, and naming the outstanding conflict count when it refuses for that
decisions.reasoning: write_output tests only result.output is None, and output is None exactly when errors is non-empty, which is SpliceResult's documented invariant -> that one test therefore reads a completed refusal and an absent run as the same thing and says 'Preview first' for both -> conflict_model.py returns the refusal reason from the held result plus the outstanding count, and the control renders it, so a refusal names the conflicts still to decide

decisions.decision: The conflict rows the run produced are rendered on the abort path in place of the bare token, and the run-wide choice is offered on the page, as the first landing increment before per-row picks exist
decisions.reasoning: conflict_rows are already computed and already returned on the abort path and the page discards them at the render -> rendering what is already returned, and passing the CLI's existing on_conflict through the page's own control, needs no core change at all -> those two land first inside the page milestone, so the operator can complete a reconstruction before the per-key mapping and the per-row picks arrive

decisions.decision: The page milestone is accepted by a served-page gate run from the gate repository exercising a conflicting collection pair end to end - preview then per-row picks then a bulk action then a write
decisions.reasoning: DL-084 records that gui/ defects are found only by serving the page - the suite's system interpreter has no nicegui and app.py is guarded by AST walk rather than by rendered DOM -> a conflict table whose rows and picks are never rendered would pass every guard this plan adds while being unusable -> the gate run is an acceptance criterion of the page milestone rather than an optional follow-up, run before the change lands

decisions.decision: ConflictRow carries a content-derived identity key - the group's sole base-input record's primary key, or the sorted tuple of the group's member primary keys where the group holds no base record - in place of the union-find root index str(key) it carries as the group label
decisions.reasoning: group_identities keys its groups on find(i), an index into the flat all_records list built as base records followed by each contribution's records in order -> that root index is positional: adding a source collection lengthens the list, shifts every later record's index, and can move a group's root, so the same track's group is labelled differently between two previews and a decision keyed on the old label attaches to a different group or to none -> the key is derived from record content instead, which is what the operator's pick is actually about, and the derivation is total: every conflicting group holds at least two records spanning at least two inputs, so both branches always yield a value

decisions.decision: A held decision survives a re-preview only when its content-derived key names a group whose member primary keys are the identical set; a group whose membership changed, and a key naming no group at all, return the row to undecided and count toward outstanding
decisions.reasoning: record_keys cascades through every tier and group_identities unions across them, so an added source can merge two previously distinct groups into one or pull a record into a group it was not in -> the operator's pick was made against the versions of one specific member set and says nothing about a set that has since grown, so re-attaching it by key alone would write a winner nobody chose for the tracks that joined -> membership is compared as a set of primary keys and only an exact match re-attaches; every other outcome is undecided, which is counted as outstanding, so a re-preview after adding a source refuses the write and shows the row again rather than silently writing a stale pick

rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: All-or-nothing for an entire run, so one edited tag forces every other track's winner too; it survives as the early unblock inside the page milestone rather than as the destination

rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Unblocks this one job and leaves the page unable to ever complete a reconstruction over a realistic collection pair

rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Needs a format, a parser and an unmatched-key report to serve an operator who is looking at rendered rows rather than a command line

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Keep ConflictRow.identity_key as the union-find root index and key decisions on it
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: The root index is positional in the flat all_records list, so adding a source shifts it and a held pick attaches to a different group or to none

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Re-attach a held decision whenever its key still names a group, without comparing membership
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: An added source can merge groups, so the pick would be applied to records it was never made against

code_intents.behavior: _resolve_conflicts takes resolutions, a mapping from an identity-group key to the token base or source, defaulting to an empty mapping. For a group whose tracked attributes diverge the mapping is consulted first: base picks the group's base-input record; source picks the group's non-base record chosen by the run-wide picker; and the group's ConflictRow records that resolution rather than the unresolved token. A divergent group the mapping does not name falls to on_conflict, and a group neither names sets unresolved and contributes a ConflictRow carrying the unresolved token. resolutions is a named keyword parameter rather than an appended positional, and every caller found by grep - assemble_output in traktor_nml/splice.py, _handle_splice in traktor_nml/commands/splice_cmd.py, the direct uses in tests/test_splice.py and the call in traktor_nml/gui/app.py - is read against the widened signature in the same change. ConflictRow carries a content-derived identity key rather than the group's union-find root index: the primary key of the group's sole base-input record where it holds one, and the sorted tuple of the group's member primary keys where it holds none. Every conflicting group spans at least two inputs and so holds at least two records, which makes the derivation total. resolutions is looked up on that same derived key, so what the mapping names is a set of records rather than a position in the flat all_records list.

assemble_output takes resolutions as a named keyword parameter defaulting to an empty mapping and hands it to _resolve_conflicts. The abort path is reached exactly when a divergent group is left undecided by both resolutions and on_conflict and returns SpliceResult with output None, errors carrying unresolved_conflicts and conflict_rows populated, before any span is rewritten, so output is None exactly when errors is non-empty. The module docstring's account of the merge names the per-key mapping alongside on_conflict as the two ways a divergence is settled and keeps DL-008's abort as what an undecided divergence does.

The splice subcommand's parser carries --on-conflict with its keep-first and keep-last choices and no resolutions argument, and _handle_splice calls assemble_output without a resolutions mapping, so the command's behaviour over any input is what it is with the parameter absent.

Guards cover a base resolution, a source resolution, a mixed run that resolves some groups and aborts on another, an empty mapping reproducing the omitted-parameter bytes, an inert unmatched resolutions key, the precedence of a per-key entry over on_conflict for its own group, and conflict_rows populated on both paths. Each guard is made to fail first and its docstring records the specific mutation applied to the module and the specific output observed under it. A further guard runs the same base collection twice - once against one source and once against that source plus a second - and asserts that the identity key of a group whose member set is unchanged is identical across both runs, and that a group whose member set the second source enlarged carries a different key.

code_intents.behavior: The module holds the operator's conflict decisions and the rows they produce and imports no nicegui and no webview, so the suite's system interpreter reaches every rule in it. A decision set maps an identity key to undecided, base or source; a key absent from the mapping reads back undecided, so a fresh set and one reset key by key behave identically. resolve sets one key; resolve_all sets every undecided key to one side and leaves an explicitly decided key standing; the resolutions projection returns only decided keys restricted to the keys the current conflict rows name, so a decision for a vanished key contributes nothing. The row projection turns a ConflictRow plus its decision into what the page renders: the identity key, the divergent attribute names, the base side's values, the source side's values and the decision. outstanding counts the undecided rows. write_refusal returns the reason a write cannot proceed - no preview held, or a held preview that refused with a named count of conflicts outstanding - and returns nothing when the held result carries output. What the tool found stays apart from what the operator said, the way review_model.py keeps status apart from decision. Re-attachment across a re-preview compares membership rather than trusting the key alone: a held decision stands only where its identity key names a group whose member primary keys are the identical set, and a key naming no group, or a group whose member set differs, leaves the row undecided and counted toward outstanding. A re-preview after a source is added therefore refuses the write and shows the affected rows again rather than applying a pick made against a member set that has since changed.

Guards cover the row projection, the three decision states, bulk resolution over a mixed decision set, the resolutions mapping's restriction to decided and still-present keys, re-attachment across a second conflict-row list, and the three write-refusal outcomes. Each guard is made to fail first and its docstring records the specific mutation applied and the specific output observed under it, matching the register tests/test_gui_wizard_state.py uses. Three further guards cover re-attachment: an unchanged member set keeps its decision; a group the added source enlarged returns to undecided and raises the outstanding count; and a key naming no group in the new rows contributes nothing to the resolutions mapping.

code_intents.behavior: The /reconstruct page holds a conflict decision set beside its base, source and result holders, so picks outlive a re-preview and are discarded with the process. preview passes the page's run-wide conflict choice as on_conflict and the decision set's resolutions projection as resolutions. On a refused run the report renders the rows conflict_model projects - one hand-rolled ui.row per conflicting track carrying the identity key, the divergent attribute names and the base and source values, with a two-state pick per row - above an all-base action, an all-source action and the outstanding count. Error tokens other than the conflict abort keep rendering as the tokens they are. The write control renders conflict_model's write_refusal reason when it refuses, so a preview that ran and refused reads differently from one that never ran, and writes the held output otherwise. Rows are hand-rolled rather than ui.aggrid, and every count, projection and decision transition is imported from conflict_model rather than computed here. The page's work is sequenced in two parts because a file belongs to one milestone. The first part depends on no core change and lands before the rest: the conflict rows rendered in place of the bare token, and the run-wide conflict choice reaching on_conflict. The second part rests on the core's derived identity key and on conflict_model, and carries the per-row picks, the bulk actions, the outstanding count and the refusal reason. A re-preview shows again, undecided, every row whose group membership the run changed. The file is read and written with newline='' so its CRLF line endings stay whole.

An AST walk over traktor_nml/gui/app.py guards what the page delegates: the conflict rendering reads conflict_model's row projection; the write refusal reads write_refusal rather than testing result.output against None; the run-wide control's choices match the splice subcommand's keep-first and keep-last; no ui.aggrid call appears; and no decision arithmetic is written inline. Each guard is made to fail first and its docstring records the specific mutation applied to app.py's source and the specific output observed under it, matching the register tests/test_gui_view_boundary.py uses.
